analysis: Design says (S40 'per-user pools that share fairly', S22; §3 G12): under a connection storm by one role another role with steady demand still obtains connections and completes operations, and overload alone does not trigger a failover. C8's rule (§10.9; kept literal by ADR-0030, LIM-25): fraction of ok cp_steady operations over each storm window ≥ 0.9, counting every storm window, also one a fault overlaps. System did: storm phase 1 (5.4–27.9 s) contained the plan's F2a on the leader (10.50 s inject, 14.21 s healed: PostgreSQL killed and restarted, leadership moved once, the only server change cp_steady saw, after the fault). 766 of 886 cp_steady operations completed ok (0.865 < 0.9) → fair-share-starvation. Every one of the 120 non-ok operations was invoked inside the F2a window (10.55–13.63 s): 114 refused at connect with 57P03, 4 refused at connect with 28P01 (password authentication failed, for a valid role, while PostgreSQL restarted), 2 info 57P01; outside that window the phase was 766 of 766 ok. Storm phase 2 (no fault) was 872 of 872 ok, and the fault-free runs (seeds 1 and 3) had 1 824 of 1 824 ok inside storms; p50/p99 latency inside storms 4.3–4.6 / 7.1–8.1 ms against 4.3–4.6 / 7.0–7.6 ms outside. Minimization (§12.2): the empty schedule PASSes (the storm alone does not starve cp_steady), the halved 45 s plan PASSes, the client-reduced plan PASSes; the original plan is the minimum and its replays FAIL with fair-share-starvation in 2 of 5 (INTERMITTENT): whether the outage's failures exceed 10 % of the storm window depends on how long PostgreSQL takes to restart. The anomaly is the unavailability window of the injected failover counted by G12's literal rule, not unfair pooling.
classification_note: Classified as §11.1 maps the guarantee: G12 → PROTOCOL_DEVIATION, severity medium (§11.2). The evidence (analysis) shows the injected failover's unavailability window counted by G12's literal rule (§10.9, ADR-0030, LIM-25), which in §11.1's terms would be a LIVENESS_OBSERVATION (severity info, finding id FND-C11-88fc04ee). Lowering the class or refining G12's rule would weaken a reported result, so it is left to the owner (closure: decision for review). The previous session's draft classified it LIVENESS_OBSERVATION; changed on resume, before any commit.

harness_review: §6.2 review of all 120 non-ok cp_steady completions in storm phase 1 (completion_review): 118 refused at connect (57P03 or 28P01 at connection startup, no statement sent: fail, row 10) and 2 with SQLSTATE 57P01 after the statement was sent (info, row 11); every ok is an acknowledged insert (row 1). The fault was confirmed and healed (nemesis events) and the run is valid. The checker applied §10.9 as written (ADR-0030 kept the literal rule; LIM-25); the classification is a triage judgement, not a checker change. Not a HARNESS_DEFECT.
known_status_reasoning: Unavailability during a failover is documented behaviour (S48: promotion 'within seconds'); no alpha-known-gap issue in RESEARCH S50 concerns pool fairness. The 28P01 refusals during the restart are recorded as an observation (NOTES §9).
origin_reasoning: The non-ok operations are connection refusals by Multigres' gateway and pooler while the leader's PostgreSQL restarted (57P03 is PostgreSQL's 'starting up'; 28P01 is returned by the gateway's authentication for a valid role). Origin MULTIGRES for the refusals; nothing points to pool unfairness.
